title: Progressive traffic-tempering and KV coalescing playbook for hosted -> dedicated switchover
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
This ticket authors a pragmatic, testable runbook to safely shift production traffic from Redwood Hosted to Dedicated capacity (and back) in the event of cross-region capacity constraints or degraded regional latency. The core failure mode we observed in prior incidents is KV cache divergence combined with untempered traffic shifts that amplify transient tail-latency and cause customer-facing request errors.

Scope and goals:
- Provide step-by-step operator actions for progressive traffic tempering (fine-grained percentage ramps) across routes, with built-in KV coalescing and health checks.
- Define automated checks, metric thresholds, and safe rollback triggers.
- Include communications templates for customer-facing escalations and internal triage.
- Provide quick remediation commands and pointers to PRs/drivers that should accompany a hotfix.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing full orchestration automation here; this is an operator playbook intended to be executable from the runbook console and run by the on-call/responsible SRE. Automation tickets will be follow-ups.
runbook_steps: 1) Initial triage: Confirm incident classification (cross-region capacity vs localized service failure). Post short summary to #incidents with region, affected services, and estimate of affected tenants.

2) Snapshot state: Capture KV meta (leader offsets, snapshot ID, last-consistent-timestamp) for both source and target regions. Archive to incident timeline with command output. This must be done before any traffic reshuffle.
3) Quiesce writes for a small tenant slice (5%): Apply write-quiesce tag on the routing layer for the slice to avoid new divergent writes during initial move.

4) Warm KV coalescing: Trigger KV coalescing job (scripts/run_kv_coalesce.sh --regions src,tgt --timeout 10m). Verify coalesce success in metrics: kv_coalesce_success_rate > 99% and kv_staleness_p99 < 5s.
5) Canary shift: Move 1-2% of read traffic for low-risk routes to Dedicated pool with target model variant. Monitor errors, p95/p99 latency, and cache miss ratio for 5 minutes.

6) Progressive tempering: If canary passes, increase traffic in steps (1->5->15->30->50) with 5-10 minute stabilization windows. Metric gates: error_rate delta < 0.2% absolute, latency increase p95 < 20% relative, kv_staleness_p99 < 10s.
7) Full coalesce: At 50% shift run a second coalesce pass to eliminate remaining divergent KV segments, confirm with snapshot comparisons and small read validations against golden dataset.
8) Final ramp or rollback: If gates hold at 50% for 30 minutes, continue to 100%. If any gate trips, rollback to prior safe percentage and open an engineering hotfix for root cause investigation.
9) Post-switchover validation: Run smoke tests across 25 representative tenants (automated script) and validate embeddings/hash parity for deterministic routes.
10) Customer communications: Use provided templates to inform affected customers of status, expected remediation windows, and available workarounds. Tag customer success and account execs.
11) Document runbook execution in incident timeline: times, outputs, who executed steps, and observed metrics. Attach artifacts (snapshots, gists, dashboards).
12) Follow-ups: Open follow-up ENG ticket to automate the tempering flow and the KV coalescing job scheduling. Include lessons learned and any missing guardrails.
rollback_plan: Immediate: Revert routing weights to last known-good percentage within 60s using routeshift tool.
If revert fails: Activate circuit-breaker on affected routes and divert to read-only fallback variant while triage continues.
Customer mitigations: Enable per-tenant rate-limits/queueing to reduce load if necessary.
Escalation: Pager to runtime-oncall -> SRE lead -> Eng on-call, and open SOC if security concerns arise.
postmortem_actions: 1) Capture exact timeline and metric deltas during shift and attach charts to the incident PM.
2) Prioritize automation tickets: automated progressive tempering + safety gates, auto-kv-coalesce orchestration.
3) Add synthetic checks that simulate partial KV divergence and ensure runbook steps would catch the failure mode.
4) Revise product docs and customer-facing KB about expected behavior during region rehome and recommended application retry logic.
5) Schedule a cross-team review with Product, Support, and Observability to validate signal coverage.
communication_templates: Internal (short): [INCIDENT] Cross-region capacity pressure. Initiating progressive traffic tempering to dedicated pool. See timeline and on-call notes.

Customer (template): We observed elevated errors affecting some requests. We're performing a staged traffic switchover to alternative capacity; you may see transient retries. We'll update in 15 minutes or when the next gate completes.
Post-incident (customer): Root cause summary, what we changed, and recommended app-side retry/backoff settings. Note SLA credits if applicable.
